_readme: REFERENCE ONLY — nothing loads this file. It exists to be read and copied from.
cars.json is the live config; it is pulled in by explicit static imports, so this
sibling file can never be picked up by accident.
One entry here mirrors one entry in cars.json exactly, so any block below can be
copy-pasted straight across. Keys starting with _ are annotations and are NOT read
by the code — drop them when you copy.
Check a model before opening a browser: npm run verify:hinges
name: BMW M5 Competition
_parts_readme: Everything in `parts` is OPTIONAL. Omit the whole block and the solver derives
the car's axes from the four Wheel_FL/FR/RL/RR empties and works out each hinge
on its own — that is the normal case and what the shipped cars.json does.
Reach for these only when a specific model comes out wrong.

_angles_readme: Opening angle per part kind, in degrees. These are the defaults; raise
doorAngleDeg for a showier reveal, lower it if doors clip a neighbouring car.
parts._durationSec_readme: Animation length for every part, in seconds.
_frame_readme: !! LAST RESORT — do NOT copy this into cars.json unless you truly need it. !!
Setting `frame` DISABLES wheel-empty detection entirely and pins the car's axes
to these world-space vectors. If you later swap in a different GLB, these stale
values silently mis-orient every hinge with no warning.
Only use it when a model's Wheel_* empties are missing or misplaced and the GLB
cannot be re-exported. Fixing the model is always the better answer.
forward = toward the front of the car, up = toward the roof, as [x, y, z].
The values below happen to be what detection already produces for this model.
Confirm with ?hinges=1: the console prints `Car frame (wheels|bounds|override)`.
_hinges_readme: Per-part overrides, keyed by the mesh name in the GLB. Valid keys:
Each entry accepts any combination of:
edge     "front" | "rear"  — which end of the CAR the hinge sits on.
Defaults: doors front, hood rear (at the
angleDeg number            — opening angle for this one part, overriding
flip     true              — reverse the opening direction.
Each example below shows a different override so you can see them in isolation.
An empty object ({}) is the normal state — see cars.json.

hinges._car_door_left_readme: angleDeg alone: this door alone swings wider than doorAngleDeg.
_car_door_right_readme: flip alone: use when a door swings INTO the cabin instead of outward.
First check ?hinges=1 — if the red axis points at the driver side rather than
the passenger side, the model's Wheel_FL/FR empties are swapped and fixing
those is the real fix. flip is the patch when the GLB can't be changed.
_car_caput_readme: edge + angleDeg: moves the hinge to the other end of the car and opens further.
A hood normally hinges at the rear (windshield end) and lifts its nose. Set
edge to "front" for a forward-tilting hood, as on some classic cars.
_car_trunk_readme: All three together. A trunk normally hinges at its front (cabin) edge and
lifts its tail; this pins the hinge at the rear instead and reverses the
swing, which is how you would model a bottom-hinged tailgate.

_defaultParts_readme: Which part option each category starts on. Values must be real ids from
car-parts.json — an unknown id logs a DynamicPart warning and falls back to stock.
_defaultPaint_readme: Starting paint per zone. Zones come from the `paintZone` userData on each
material in the GLB (body | trim | interior); materials without it default to body.
metalness/roughness/clearcoat are standard PBR values in the 0..1 range.
_defaultSuspension_readme: Ride-height offset in centimetres. 0 is stock, negative lowers, positive raises.
